question: A steel scale is correct at $0°$C. A length measured with it at $40°$C reads $50.00$ cm. If $\alpha_{steel} = 1.2 \times 10^{-5}\ °\text{C}^{-1}$, the true length is
solution:
At $40°$C each scale division has expanded, so the true length is larger than the reading:
$$L = 50(1 + 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \times 40) = 50.024\ \text{cm}$$
